```sql
WITH item_sales AS (
  SELECT
    i_manager_id,
    ss_item_sk,
    ss_sales_price,
    d_moy AS month_of_year
  FROM
    item
    JOIN store_sales ON ss_item_sk = i_item_sk
    JOIN date_dim ON ss_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk
    JOIN store ON ss_store_sk = s_store_sk
  WHERE
    d_month_seq IN (1222, 1222 + 1, ..., 1222 + 11)
),
monthly_sales AS (
  SELECT
    manager_id,
    month_of_year,
    AVG(ss_sales_price) OVER (PARTITION BY manager_id) AS avg_monthly_sales
  FROM
    item_sales
  GROUP BY
    manager_id,
    month_of_year
),
anomalies AS (
  SELECT
    manager_id,
    month_of_year,
    CASE
      WHEN avg_monthly_sales > 0 THEN
        ABS(sum_sales - avg_monthly_sales) / avg_monthly_sales
      ELSE NULL
    END AS anomaly_score
  FROM
    monthly_sales
    JOIN (
      SELECT
        manager_id,
        SUM(ss_sales_price) AS sum_sales
      FROM
        item_sales
      GROUP BY
        manager_id
    ) AS sales_sum ON monthly_sales.manager_id = sales_sum.manager_id
  WHERE
    anomaly_score > 0.1
)
SELECT * FROM anomalies ORDER BY manager_id, avg_monthly_sales, sum_sales LIMIT 100;
```

This version of the query separates the filtering conditions from the JOIN clauses and groups them together to reduce the number of intermediate results. It also avoids using subqueries in the SELECT clause, which can lead to performance issues due to repeated evaluations. The CTEs (common table expressions) are defined with explicit aliases for each output column.
